newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong gears up to expand debt market - Tsang.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gears up to expand debt market - Tsang.

text.p: Hong Kong is poised to expand its debt market with plans to set up a mandatory retirement fund and a mortgage corporation, Financial Secretary Donald Tsang said on Tuesday.

"Hong Kong will soon see the implementation of the Mandatory Provident Fund (MPF) System for our workforce... (which) will cover more than two million people in the workforce," Tsang said at a dinner speech.
"It will generate a significant increase to the retirement reserves. The estimated annual contributions under the system will amount to about HK$30-40 billion," he said.
The large pool of reserves would hike demand for investment vehicles, in particular, for instruments producing steady income over the long term to match underlying retirement liabilities.

The fund, a testimony to Hong Kong's high savings ratio, would spur development of hedging instruments, Tsang said. While the size of Hong Kong's debt market was admittedly small compared with its equity and banking sectors, total outstanding public and private sector debt issues have increased eight-fold, from HK$27 billion at end-1989 to HK$236 billion by September 1996.
Tsang also said the government, while performing its regulatory role over the MPF, would not interfere excessively.
"The government is clear in its objective that there should not be a regulatory overkill," he said.
"We will seek to strike the right balance between protecting the MPF assets and allowing the investment managers sufficient flexibility to maximize the yield," he said.
Tsang also suggested massive projects in burgeoning East Asian economies as a possible channel of investments.

"The World Bank has estimated that the funding needs of infrastructure in East Asia amount to US$1.5 trillion in the next decade. China alone is estimated to account for half of this amount," he said.
As for Hong Kong's plan to set up a mortgage corporation, Tsang said it would promote stability in the banking and monetary sectors, as well as facilitate home ownership.

"The Mortgage Corporation will provide high quality debt paper for investments and widen the range of financial products being offered, including fixed rate paper and mortgaged-backed securities," he said.
He said the corporation would initially be fully owned by the government, increasing chances of its acceptability.
The corporation would operate as a wholesale financial intermediary, mainly purchasing residential mortgages from authorized institutions in line with a set of criteria.
